title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Errors by Opposing Counsel
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: Opposing counsel sends over a drafted settlement agreement for a breach of contract matter. The paralegal notices opposing counsel made a typographical error in the mathematics, inserting $15,000 instead of the agreed-upon $5,000. What must the paralegal do?
options: Tell their client to sign it immediately to secure the extra $10,000.
Notify opposing counsel of the obvious error before executing the agreement.
Alter the document to correct the math error and send it back signed without explanation.
Withdraw from the file due to the opponent's incompetence.
questions.explain: Under the duty of Good Faith and Civility (Rule 2.01), a paralegal must not take advantage of an obvious mistake or slip by opposing counsel. Taking advantage of a clear typographical error in a drafted agreement is sharp practice. The paralegal must notify the drafter.
